purpose: Current browser-platform source check for rev0202 runtime-core recovery-guidance refactor and storage posture non-claims.
scope: Runtime-core storage recovery guidance should stay small because browser storage/platform caveats keep growing.
FROST OPFS SSD timing/privacy review posture

sources.finding: OPFS is origin-private storage, quota-bound, exposed through navigator.storage.getDirectory(), and cleared when site storage is cleared.
Browser storage quota/eviction behavior is browser- and policy-dependent; estimate() is planning input, not reservation.
AbortSignal can reject a lock request if it fires before grant; once a lock is granted, the signal is ignored by the lock manager.
Storage Buckets offer more granular storage/eviction management in Chromium capability space; they are not a BrowserRT baseline guarantee.
FROST presents OPFS-backed SSD timing/fingerprinting research; BrowserRT should keep large OPFS writes behind privacy review and avoid mitigation claims.

appliedToThisTurn: Kept platform commentary out of runtime-core code paths and encoded recovery classes as data tables instead of branching prose.
Ratchet runtime-core closure after reducing bytes so later storage posture work has a hard fail signal before budget exhaustion.
Preserved privacy/storage non-claims and browser posture proofs rather than expanding public API doctrine.
nonClaims: This research artifact is not a browser compatibility matrix, legal/security review, Storage Buckets implementation, or claim that BrowserRT mitigates OPFS timing side channels.
